questions.text:
Which of the following languages is/are regular?
[latex]L_{1}:\{wxw^{R}|w,x \in \{a,b\}^{*} \; and \; |w|,|x| \gt 0 \}, w^{R}[/latex] is the reverse of string w
[latex]L_{2}:\{a^{n}b^{m}|m\neq n \; and \; m,n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{3}:\{a^{p}b^{q}c^{r}|p,q,r\geq 0\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- L1: since x can be anything, it is enough that the first and last symbols match (w of length 1). L1 = a(a+b)+a + b(a+b)+b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.
- L2: [latex]a^nb^m[/latex] with [latex]m\ne n[/latex] needs counting [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not regular.
- L3 = a*b*c* [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.

Answer: L1 and L3 only

questions.text:
Given below are some algorithms, and some algorithm design paradigms.

Match the above algorithms on the left to the corresponding design paradigm they follow.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Dijkstra: greedy (iii)
- Floyd-Warshall: dynamic programming (ii)
- Binary search: divide and conquer (i)
- Backtracking: depth-first search (iv)

Answer: 1-iii, 2-ii, 3-i, 4-iv

questions.text:
A Young tableau is a 2D array of integers increasing from left to right and from top to bottom. Any unfilled entries are marked with [latex]\infty[/latex], and hence there cannot be any entry to the right of, or below a [latex]\infty[/latex]. The following Young tableau consists of unique entries.

When an element is removed from a Young tableau, other elements should be moved into its place so that the resulting table is still a Young tableau (unfilled entries may be filled in with a [latex]\infty[/latex]). The minimum number of entries (other than 1) to be shifted, to remove 1 from the given Young tableau is _______.
questions.solution:
Removing 1 leaves a hole. Repeatedly fill it with the smaller of its right and lower neighbour:

- hole (1,1): min(2, 3) = 2 moves left
- hole (1,2): min(5, 4) = 4 moves up
- hole (2,2): min(6, 12) = 6 moves left
- hole (2,3): min(23, 18) = 18 moves up
- hole (3,3): min(25, [latex]\infty[/latex]) = 25 moves left
- hole (3,4) gets [latex]\infty[/latex]

Shifted: 2, 4, 6, 18, 25 = 5 entries

Answer: 5

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

The pivot is at index left_end and is the (left_end + 1)-th smallest.

- If left_end + 1 [latex]\gt[/latex] k: search the left part a[0 .. left_end[latex]-[/latex]1] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (a, left_end, k)
- Else: search the right part starting at a + left_end + 1, with n [latex]-[/latex] left_end [latex]-[/latex] 1 elements, for the (k [latex]-[/latex] left_end [latex]-[/latex] 1)-th smallest

Answer: (a, left_end, k) and (a+left_end+1, n-left_end-1, k-left_end-1)

questions.text: Which one of the following hash functions on integers will distribute keys most uniformly over 10 buckets numbered 0 to 9 for i ranging from 0 to 2020?
questions.solution:
Last digit of [latex]i^3[/latex] for last digits 0..9: 0, 1, 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 9. Every bucket gets used equally.

Squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, so options 1, 3, 4 leave some buckets empty.

Answer: h(i) = [latex]i^3[/latex] mod 10
